title: SDK-level disconnect handshake for hybrid tool-call streaming
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Recent incidents and load tests show a class of production problems when clients disconnect mid-stream while the generation is performing tool/function calls or emitting structured outputs. Problems include: partial JSON blobs left in KV/prefix cache, tool-call fences that are left open (external side effects attempted twice or never), and poor UX when the same client resumes without clear determinism. Server heuristics (timeout-based GC) are currently too coarse — they either discard usable partial output quickly or retain it too long, increasing memory and KV pressure.

Objective: Implement a server+SDK handshake to make client disconnects deterministic and low-cost for hybrid streams (generations that interleave token streaming, structured output delimiters, and function/tool calls). The handshake will allow graceful-detach, soft-checkpoint, and explicit finalizer ACK semantics while providing a compat shim for older clients and an automatic fallback path for unknown clients.
proposal: High-level approach: 1) SDKs (web, node, python) expose an explicit "gracefulDetach()" API that attempts a 500–1500ms handshake before closing network transport. 2) Protocol: add an optional HTTP/WS header and streaming message types: resume-intent, soft-checkpoint, finalizer-ack. 3) Server state machine: track ephemeral generation sessions with granular lifecycle states: Active, Soft-Checkpointed, Quarantine, Tombstoned. 4) Tool-call fences: when a tool call is in-flight, the server will record a function-call fence and enter Soft-Checkpointed; an explicit finalizer-ack from client transitions the fence to Closed. 5) Compatibility layer: servers accept legacy clients but use heuristics to create soft-checkpoints at token boundaries and conservatively tombstone after TTL. 6) Cache retention: keep KV/prefix cache for soft-checkpointed sessions for configurable window (default 1 minute) and provide expedited compaction when memory pressure spikes.
api_changes: Protocol additions (flat-string summary): - HTTP/WS header: X-Redwood-Resume-Intent: true|false - Stream control events: {type: 'soft_checkpoint', checkpoint_id: '<uuid>', meta: 'structured|funccall'}; {type: 'finalizer_ack', checkpoint_id: '<uuid>'}; {type: 'resume_request', checkpoint_id: '<uuid>'} - SDK: gracefulDetach(timeoutMs=1000) returns checkpoint_id or null - Resume flow: client supplies resume_request with checkpoint_id and (optionally) a partial-output hash for integrity checks. Server responds with resume_accepted|resume_conflict|resume_expired. - Backward compatibility: if header absent or client pre-Handshake, server emits server-side soft_checkpoints and includes a best-effort checkpoint_id in the stream footer.
compatibility: Older clients: server will operate in legacy mode where it infers checkpoints at function-call boundaries and JSON-structural boundaries. For older clients we add a 'compat-checkpoint' footer message so resumed requests from modern SDKs can claim ownership of a near-checkpoint. SDK migration plan: roll SDK updates with grace period; server toggles strict-checkpoint mode per-tenant via a feature flag. Edge cases: mobile SDKs that cannot wait on gracefulDetach will fall through to heuristics; document tradeoffs clearly.
data_retention_policy: Defaults: soft-checkpoint retention: 1 minute; quarantine TTL: 5 minutes; tombstone permanent marker kept for 7 days for auditing (small footprint). Values can be overridden per-customer on Dedicated/Private. Metrics-based eviction: if memory pressure > 80%, server will compact earliest soft-checkpoints first. All durations are configurable via runtime flags and console UI (ops can set per-organization).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): server feature-flag on 10% runtime nodes; publish SDK v1.18 (node, python, web) with gracefulDetach behind opt-in flag. Run synthetic tests and smoke customers. Phase 2 (wider canary): enable SDK by default for new SDKs, keep server feature-flag opt-out for legacy tenants. Phase 3: enable server strict-checkpointing by default for hosted; announce migration and provide a 30-day compatibility window for Dedicated/Private customers. Include kill-switch in console. Rollback plan: disable strict-checkpoint server flag; SDKs fallback to legacy heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: SDK gracefulDetach successfully returns checkpoint_id within configured timeout in >= 99% of test cases
Resume flow deterministic: resume_accepted is returned only when checkpoint matches partial-output hash
No duplicate tool invocation occurs for resumed sessions in integration tests
Memory pressure tests show soft-checkpoint retention cost within budget (<= 7% memory overhead under 99th percentile traffic)
Compatibility: legacy clients continue to receive valid streams and server emits compat-checkpoint footer
tests: Integration: simulated abrupt disconnect during function-call; verify no double-invoke after resume
Load: high-throughput streaming with many short-lived soft-checkpoints, ensure eviction LRU behavior
Chaos: kill node during finalizer_ack path and ensure resume_conflict handled gracefully
SDK e2e: web SDK gracefulDetach under flaky network at 250ms/500ms/1000ms timeouts
docs: Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/STREAM/SDK+Disconnect+Handshake (internal). SDK design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/streaming/handshake-sdk-design. Migration announcement draft: /docs/migration/graceful-detach.md
notes: Implementation notes: - Use existing session store (lease token metadata) to record checkpoint_id and minimal pointer to KV/prefix cache; avoid duplicating large blobs. - For function-call fences we should record an idempotency-key and require tool adapters to support idempotency or provide compensating actions. - Keep TTLs conservative initially; we can reduce retention after monitoring. - Coordinate with Console (PM) to expose per-tenant TTLs and a toggle for strict-checkpoint mode. - Follow-on work: expose 'checkpoint recovery inspector' in Console and a debug API to force-finalize a quarantined session.
